finding.claim: MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH is not enforced for chunked request bodies (no Content-Length), allowing unbounded buffering to memory or temp files until BODY_TIMEOUT expires.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP client sending a chunked request body (Transfer-Encoding: chunked, no Content-Length) to any route that reads request.form, request.files, or get_data().
finding.sink: request.body queue (asgi.py:65 put) and file-part streaming to temp files (formparser.py:205-208), plus full in-memory buffering in Body.__await__ (request.py:99-106).

trace.note: handle_messages pushes every http.request chunk into request.body.put() with no byte accounting
Length check only sets _must_raise when a declared Content-Length exceeds the limit; absent header means no check
Body.__anext__ checks only _must_raise, never a running total, so streaming multipart parsing is unbounded
_parse_multipart iterates the body via async for, i.e. __anext__, and writes file parts to a temp file via start_file_streaming
Body.__await__ buffers the full body before checking the total against max_content_length, so the 413 fires only after memory is consumed
BODY_TIMEOUT=60 bounds per-request parse duration, not bytes received

finding.guards_checked: Content-Length pre-check (request.py:65-70) only applies to declared lengths. MAX_FORM_MEMORY_SIZE (app.py:232) caps only non-file field data. MAX_FORM_PARTS (app.py:233) caps part count, not size. BODY_TIMEOUT (app.py:226, request.py:288, :352-360) limits duration only. Werkzeug multipart decoder internals were assumed, not verified, since werkzeug is not vendored in the repo. No dynamic repro was run; verified by reading only.
